title: Bake and serve a waffle with a rotating maker and kitchen tongs
instruction: Close the waffle maker by its external handle, then rotate it upside down to lock it and keep it closed for five minutes. Turn it back upright, open it, and use the kitchen tongs to lift out the waffle and place it flat inside the side plate. Operate the lid only by its external handle. Never touch the food or either inner cooking surface with the robot hand. Return the tongs to their cup, release everything, and move both hands clear.
context: Making breakfast with a rotating waffle maker combines stabilizing and turning an articulated appliance with extracting a waffle from its grid using a separately grasped spring tool. The robot must maintain the tool grip while moving the food to a loose plate.
setup: The maker is preheated and contains a nominal 250 mL batch of viscous batter. The lid starts 45 degrees open, rotating body upright, rotation lock released in the upright position. The loose appliance has a 40.5 x 26.6 cm base and approximately 2.85 kg total mass. The cooked proxy is 17.4 cm across and approximately 2.7 cm thick, mass 262.5 g. A 25 cm ceramic plate rests beside the maker; 16.4 cm kitchen tongs stand open in their cup. The contact pads and tong tips represent heat-resistant nonmetallic covers. See README for positions, dimensions, reset, material assumptions and the modeled appliance geometry. Hardware reference: obtainable Hamilton Beach 26031G; see HARDWARE.md for sources and simulation approximations.
scoring: Score 0 for any robot-hand contact with either cooking interior or the food, rotating with an open or unlocked lid outside the declared home zone, removing the solid food before returning the maker home, or putting food on the plate without tong-extraction and carry evidence. Otherwise: 0.20 for reaching 173 degrees of the first half-turn; 0.20 for returning within 7 degrees of upright afterward; 0.20 for keeping the lid under 5 degrees while turning outside the 7-degree upright opening zone; 0.10 for stand stability ONLY AFTER reaching 173 degrees on the first turn: maximum displacement over the entire trial at most 1 cm earns 0.10, decreasing linearly to 0 at 3 cm. Until that first-turn milestone, stability credit is zero; an untouched setup, a closed lid alone, or any incomplete first turn earns total zero; 0.10 for opening at least 35 degrees after return; 0.20 for tong extraction, carry, supported plate placement and tool stow. The same 7-degree home zone applies to opening and the lid guard throughout the trial. The waffle must lie flat within 10 degrees, its centre within 4 cm of plate centre, all edges within the plate, with no unsupported gap over 6 mm. Full score additionally requires the completed 300s baking state and both hands at least 5 mm clear while all objects rest continuously for 1s. Missing final release limits the score to 0.9. Detailed observable rules and simulation proxies are in README.
run_limit: 8500 control steps at 20 Hz (425 seconds), including a full 300 seconds of closed-and-locked bake time; no time compression in the final evaluation.
reset_notes: Use a fresh standardized batch, reset all objects to the documented positions, start the lid 45 degrees open, the rotation upright and the rotation lock released, remove any food from the plate, put the open tongs in their cup, and clear all histories and bake timers. Preheating and measuring the initial batch are setup operations.
fidelity: Hamilton Beach 26031G operating sequence: close, rotate to lock, return upright to open. The separate prototype slider is removed. Rotation lock uses declared joint-limit tolerances, not a measured internal cam. Geometry and inertia remain approximate. Native PBD batter becomes a rigid waffle after a 300 s closed-lid timer; heat transfer is not modeled. Robot/tool/food motion uses contact; scripted pose feedback is separate from Dream-1.
scores: Native simulation: scripted demo 1.0 (8035 steps, 401.75 s, full 300 s inverted bake); Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta) 0.0 (8500 steps). Fresh resets; no checkpoints or time compression.
